Q088.fact_true: "Not all lobsters are red" says that it is not the case that every lobster is red, so the negation applies to a universal claim about lobsters, and "all" claims are conditionals.
Q088.fact_false: Saying "not all lobsters are red" is the same as saying there are no red lobsters, which is a negated existential statement about things that are both lobsters and red.
Q088.method: Write the sentence as "it is not true that every lobster is red," then check which option places the negation outside a universal quantifier with the right connective for "all."

Q089.fact_true: In standard predicate-logic translation, a proper name like Sheena is represented by a lowercase constant, and the predicate letter is written before the constant.
Q089.fact_false: In predicate logic the name is written first as a lowercase constant and then the predicate letter, so the subject comes before the property being attributed.
Q089.method: Identify which letter stands for the predicate and which for the individual, then check which option puts the predicate letter first followed by the lowercase constant.

Q100.fact_true: A uniform solid disk has moment of inertia (1/2)MR², and rolling without slipping means v = ωR, so translational and rotational kinetic energy are both proportional to Mv².
Q100.fact_false: When a disk rolls without slipping, its kinetic energy splits equally between translation and rotation, because the speed of the center equals the speed of the rim.
Q100.method: Compute translational KE as (1/2)Mv² and rotational KE as (1/2)Iω² with I = (1/2)MR² and ω = v/R, then divide rotational KE by the sum.
